title: Paradism as the canon's proposed economy
statement: The canon proposes a post-scarcity, fully automated, moneyless society — later systematized in the movement's vocabulary as paradism — modeled on the Elohim's own home-world economy, in which machines perform necessary labor and human beings are freed for thought, creation, and fulfillment; this record carries the proposal as the canon's explicit normative content, with the incentive, transition, and feasibility objections carried at full strength.

includes: The proposal as the canon states it: full automation of necessary labor, abolition of money and wage-work, the home-world economy as the model witnessed in the second message
Its position in the framework: the socio-economic form of the anticipated Golden Age, within the period claims (woh-claim-0015)
The vocabulary note: 'paradism' as the movement's later systematization of canon-stated content — the term's history kept distinct from the proposal's
The reception layer: incentive, transition-path, and automation-feasibility objections, and the family relationship to terrestrial post-scarcity thought, preserved without flattening
excludes: Endorsement or implementation advocacy by the corpus
Economic forecasting; no automation timeline is asserted
Identification with any terrestrial political program; family resemblance to post-work thought is context, not equivalence
The movement's paradism campaigns, which are organizational history

source_references.locator: The home-world economy account: automated labor, absence of money, the freed life witnessed
The first message's automation-and-liberation material within the New Commandments frame
The academic treatment of the movement's economic doctrine

alternatives.statement: Moneyless full automation lacks an account of allocation and motivation; the proposal names an end-state without an economics.
No path from present economies to the end-state is specified; the proposal is utopian in the technical sense.
The home-world economy is the era's automation utopianism projected onto the visitors; the 1970s provenance shows in the details.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0020 is revised in a way that affects the provenance.
The canon's fuller context changes the economy's description.
Public prose begins forecasting automation timelines or merging the proposal with terrestrial programs, both of which this record excludes.
